title: Strategic Game In Normal Form
body_html:
Strategic Game In Normal Form

A strategic game in normal form is data $$ G=(I,(S_i)_{i\in I},(g_i)_{i\in I}) $$ where $I$ is a nonempty finite set of players, each $S_i$ is a nonempty strategy set, and each payoff function is $$ g_i:\prod_{j\in I} S_j \to \mathbb R. $$ For a strategy profile $s=(s_i)_{i\in I}$, $g_i(s)$ is player $i$'s utility from the profile.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 1.3.1] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Normal-form strategic game defined by players, strategy sets, and payoff functions.
  • [MFoGT, Section 4.2] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Chapter 4 notation G = (I,(S_i),(g_i)).
